title: The engagement record: each walk as a piece of work done for someone
request: Collect the knowledge of giving the service.
plan: One ServiceEngagement per walk, linked to its build.
A walk that stopped in the draft says so.

findings.defect: Every kept version of a walk became its own engagement.
findings.scenario: A draft kept before and after its build gave two engagements, one 'stopped'.
findings.fix: The current chain only: a snapshot's newest version.

findings.defect: The backfill kept no walks, so no engagement was built.
findings.scenario: python -m dclab_rnd.store run over 800 workspaces: walks read 0.
findings.cause: The walks keeper read only a running server's services.
findings.fix: Without a server, each file workspace's walks are read from its folder (its project, draft, ledger and event stores, opened only where the folder exists, nothing written).

findings.defect: An engagement's request, expectation, explanation and feedback were always unknown.
findings.scenario: 874 engagements, each with four parts unknown.
findings.fix: The draft's own record (the person's first words, its questions answered or not, its brief), the final record's notes, limits and interval, and feedback.given events by draft or project.

outcome: Every walk is an engagement, delivered or stopped.
lessons: Write fixtures from the code that writes the records (a stage record copied from the engine), never from memory: invented shapes made every test pass while every real build was judged wrong.
